citation: Kroenke, K., Spitzer, R. L., & Williams, J. B. W. (2001). The PHQ-9: Validity of a brief depression severity measure. Journal of General Internal Medicine, 16(9), 606-613.
description: A nine-item screen for the severity of depressive symptoms over the last two weeks.

bands.description: Minimal or no depressive symptoms. No action is needed on this screen alone.
bands.label: Minimal

bands.description: Mild depressive symptoms. Talk to a doctor or a mental health professional if the symptoms last.
bands.label: Mild

bands.description: Moderate depressive symptoms. This range is a reason to talk to a doctor or a mental health professional.
bands.label: Moderate

bands.description: Moderately severe depressive symptoms. Seek an assessment from a doctor or a mental health professional.
bands.label: Moderately severe

bands.description: Severe depressive symptoms. Seek help now, and call a crisis line if you are in danger.
bands.label: Severe

domains.description: How severe the depressive symptoms are, summed over the nine items.
domains.high: A higher score means more of the symptoms in the last two weeks.
domains.low: A lower score means fewer of the symptoms in the last two weeks.
domains.name: Depression severity

evidence.limitations: This is a screen, not a diagnosis. It records how you describe the last two weeks, so it can change from week to week. A clinician makes a diagnosis, and only with more information than a questionnaire.

validity.summary: A score of 10 or more detects major depression with a sensitivity of 88 percent and a specificity of 88 percent in the development sample.

info.audience: Adults who want a short, structured look at how they have been feeling.
info.authors: Kurt Kroenke, Robert L. Spitzer, and Janet B. W. Williams
notFor: A screen for every mental health concern.
info.responseScale: A four-point frequency scale, from Not at all to Nearly every day.
whatYouGet: The published severity band for that score.
A link that shares your result and a file that saves it.

instructions: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by each of the following problems? Answer for how you have actually been, not how you would like to be.

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things.
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much.
Feeling tired or having little energy.
Feeling bad about yourself, or that you are a failure, or that you have let yourself or your family down.
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading a newspaper or watching television.
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed, or the opposite: being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual.
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way.
